messages:
lee: Quick design check — thinking about swapping the heatmap gradient to a semi-opaque neon overlay instead of the current solid band. Problem: it looks poppy but might reduce text/chart axis contrast. Thoughts?

jess: I like the idea for density legibility, but worried about accessibility. can you paste the color tokens? :eyes:

lee: sure — current tokens: `--heat-low: #0f1724`, `--heat-mid: #1f2a3b`, `--heat-high: #3b82f6`. proposed: `--heat-low: rgba(10,14,20,0.6)`, `--heat-mid: rgba(59,130,246,0.14)`, `--heat-high: rgba(99,102,241,0.3)`

matt: hmmm the mid/high both sit in the blue family, which will collide with our link color (`--link: #3b82f6`). if heat uses blue too much, line charts and annotations disappear. maybe shift to a warm accent for high density? :warning:

ani: agree with matt. also syntax highlighting for code blocks in dark mode uses blue for keys, so JSON diffs will feel wrong. proposal: keep mid-blue but push high -> magenta/orange (e.g., `#ff6b6b` or `#f59e0b`) so it reads as an overlay, not a semantic link.

sam: accessibility nit: any overlay approach needs to pass 4.5:1 for axis/label contrast. currently with semi-opaque overlays the labels drop below 3:1 in our test harness. we should run the contrast checker on final comps.

aria: small UX point — for keyboard users, heatmap cells need a clear focus ring. if we add neon overlay it must not obscure the focus stroke. Suggest focus be `--focus: 2px solid #ffffff20` and ensure z-order.

lee: good call. Actionable plan: 1) try `--heat-high` as `#f59e0b` at 0.28 alpha, 2) run contrast checks on axis/labels + keyboard focus, 3) update syntax palette so keys aren't same hue as heat high. i'll put a quick Figma frame.

jess: can you also add an alternative with gradient-to-transparent instead of opaque overlay? some charts look cleaner with a radial fade.

contrast-bot: automated check results (preliminary): axis text on proposed frame = 3.1:1, labels on hover = 2.7:1, focus ring = 5.6:1. Recommendation: increase label weight or move labels off overlay.

matt: thanks bot. if label weight up is easier (bold 600) that's a quick win. Also re: syntax — i'll propose a token set that reserves `--accent-1` for links/interactive, `--accent-2` for heat high, and `--accent-3` for chart series. keeps semantics separate.

ani: one more UX tweak — for stacked area charts, the overlay can create moiré on thin lines. consider reducing opacity on small height buckets (< 16px) to avoid banding.

lee: all excellent. i'll mock 3 variants (blue->magenta, blue->orange, radial fade) and attach screenshots. tagging @design for quick eyes before Friday demo. :thumbsup:
